audits.claim: Error timestamps in seconds are compared directly with rrweb timestamps in milliseconds, putting errors before earlier breadcrumbs.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/eventstore/models.py:117-118 interprets the stored event timestamp as epoch seconds, while tests/sentry/replays/unit/test_event_parser.py:329-333 demonstrates millisecond top-level recording timestamps. src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:115 copies the stored timestamp unchanged and :153-158 compares it directly with the recording timestamp; reader.py:271-281 supplies the raw segment without conversion. For a breadcrumb at 1700000000000 ms and a later error at 1700000001 seconds, the comparison yields the error first; :177 sends that incorrect ordering to Seer.

audits.claim: Boolean(normalizedDateRange) is always true and adds no query gating.
audits.evidence: static/app/components/organizations/pageFilters/parse.tsx:213-272 always returns Object.fromEntries(paramEntries), including for an empty result, and defaults the period at :255-256. Consequently static/app/components/feedback/list/useFeedbackSummary.tsx:36-38 is gated only by the feature flag. The redundant condition is real, but no invalid request or missing required date guard follows because normalization supplies the default period.

audits.claim: Merged-PR comment construction performs a sequential recommended-event lookup for each issue.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:401-412 and src/sentry/integrations/gitlab/integration.py:249-260 synchronously call get_environment_info for each issue. src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:585-590 invokes get_recommended_event, whose normal non-expired path queries get_events_snql at src/sentry/models/group.py:305-315 and may additionally fall back to the latest event at :881-890. However the actual task selects only the top five issues at src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/tasks.py:134-147, so this is a bounded extra-query cost for the added environment information, without a demonstrated timeout or wrong result.

audits.claim: The new hidden-attribute filter is bypassed whenever the search query is empty.
audits.evidence: static/app/views/performance/newTraceDetails/traceDrawer/details/span/eapSections/attributes.tsx:51 initializes an empty search and :60-63 returns sorted attributes before applying HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES at :65-68. sortAttributes in traceDrawer/details/utils.tsx:98-110 only copies and sorts, so an input attribute named project_id remains visible in the default state and is passed to AttributesTree at attributes.tsx:135-139. Typing project removes that same attribute through the new filter, making the intended hiding inconsistent and ineffective on initial display.

audits.claim: The Flex replacements omit the previous center alignment and spacing in the tabs/vitals row and second placeholder group.
audits.evidence: The supplied diff removes Container/FlexBox with align-items:center and gap:space(1); static/app/views/performance/newTraceDetails/traceTabsAndVitals.tsx:93 supplies only justify, and :27 supplies neither align nor gap. static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:18-25 adds no defaults for either property, confirming the lost CSS. In the loading state the three equal-height 100px placeholders at traceTabsAndVitals.tsx:28-30 now touch rather than retaining gaps; this is a concrete but cosmetic layout regression, without evidence of functional breakage.

audits.claim: Removing height:100% from the waterfall wrapper can prevent it from filling its parent.
audits.evidence: The height declaration is removed, but both actual callers contradict the proposed non-flex-parent failure: static/app/views/performance/newTraceDetails/index.tsx:137-152 wraps TraceWaterfall in TabsWaterfallWrapper, defined as a flex column with flex:1 1 100% at :173-176. The replay caller at static/app/views/replays/detail/trace/trace.tsx:152-168 uses TraceViewWaterfallWrapper, a flex column with height:100% at :184-188. The new waterfall root at traceWaterfall.tsx:712 has flex:1, which flex.tsx:25 applies to fill available main-axis space in these parents; no failing caller is established.

audits.claim: The attribute-key hook drops explicit query options and environment, and reports background fetching as loading.
audits.evidence: static/app/views/explore/hooks/useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:50-61 does omit the former options and maps isLoading to isFetching; useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:42-50 deliberately omits environment. However static/app/utils/queryClient.tsx:19-24 already disables refetchOnWindowFocus globally, so dropping that override does not enable focus refetching, and the hook uses the same underlying useQuery as useApiQuery (:125-128). The retry override is genuinely lost, but neither retries nor background loading alone establishes incorrect behavior; this is a behavior/intent clarification rather than a traced functional defect.

audits.claim: The new story contains the duplicated word "the the".
audits.evidence: static/app/views/dashboards/widgets/tableWidget/tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx:28 contains "Below is the the most basic example" in the Getting Started paragraph. The supplied diff adds this story, so the typo is introduced here and affects documentation only.

audits.claim: The rewritten browser-report endpoint tests no longer exercise application/reports+json parsing.
audits.evidence: tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_browser_reporting_collector.py:67 and :91 post without a content_type; src/sentry/conf/server.py:1831 sets the test request default format to json. The remaining explicit media type at test_browser_reporting_collector.py:79 is intentionally invalid, and the diff removes the two application/reports+json posts. src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:69,82 still registers the custom parser, so this is lost test coverage rather than a demonstrated production parsing failure.

audits.claim: The new project-not-found branch can flash during the replay page initial project-store load.
audits.evidence: Although static/app/utils/useProjectFromId.tsx:7-12 itself does not distinguish loading, the containing replay flow does: useReplayData.tsx:104,122-126 cannot fetch recording attachments without a project slug, obtained by the same project-store lookup in useReplayProjectSlug.tsx:10-17. ReplayDetailsPage at static/app/views/replays/detail/page.tsx:34-35 renders ReplayLayout with isLoading during loading, and replayLayout.tsx:73-80 replaces FocusArea (and thus Ai) with a placeholder. If missing project data leaves an empty recording after other requests finish, replayReader.tsx:436-447 flags processing errors and replayLoadingState.tsx:67-71 renders that error before the AI content; the proposed initial-load alert path is therefore blocked.

audits.claim: Seconds-based recording fixtures conceal the real seconds-versus-milliseconds error-interleaving defect.
audits.evidence: tests/sentry/replays/test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:188,254 use now.timestamp() for top-level recording timestamps and :290,298 use 1.5 and 2.0; :305-331 checks ordering against errors at 1.0 and 3.0. By contrast tests/sentry/replays/unit/test_event_parser.py:329 uses a millisecond top-level timestamp, and src/sentry/eventstore/models.py:117-118 treats error timestamps as seconds. Substituting 1500 and 2000 for the unit-test breadcrumbs makes both errors precede hello at project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:153-158, instead of the asserted placement of the 3-second error after world; this is the same production unit-mismatch root cause as finding 1.

audits.claim: The renamed TopNEventsSpans test class actually populates the events/transactions dataset rather than spans.
audits.evidence: tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py:1250 renames the class to OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans, but :1260-1264 loads a transaction and :1264-1333 builds message/fingerprint events. The fixtures are stored using store_event at :1335-1342, and :1347-1365 exercises organization-events-stats without selecting a spans dataset. The diff changes the name without changing those fixtures, so the naming is misleading but the existing test behavior is unaffected.
